tickets.summary: NDE bearing vibration rose from 2.1 to 4.6 mm/s in six weeks and has not plateaued, though below alarm; failure of this single export train would cut production within an hour.
tickets.recommended_action: Rotating equipment specialist inspect today; diagnose and correct findings, then verify vibration stabilizes below alarm. Diagnose bearing vibration mechanism. Obtain source-required attention today. Update vibration trend and alarm margin.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: A strong, continuing bearing-vibration increase with growing spectral components supports high near-term failure likelihood, but it remains below alarm and function loss is not confirmed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: K-3401 is a single export train with no spare or workaround; a trip sends the platform to recycle and cuts production within an hour.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed its first test start, then started after 8 s and reached rated pressure; recurrent starting issues and uncertain FW-8101 delivery degrade firewater resilience.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect batteries and starting-air system; correct confirmed defects, then prove first-attempt start and rated discharge pressure. Check impairment deviation record. Prove first-attempt start performance. Test FW-8101 pressure and flow. Test batteries and starting air.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Failure on the first test attempt confirms loss of the required start-on-demand function. The successful second attempt and normal run bound the failure but do not erase it.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure removes one safety-critical firewater pump from dependable demand service. FW-8101 is designated as its redundant partner, but its later 9.2 barg result and unmeasured flow prevent crediting it as fully capable.

tickets.summary: Pump A delivered 9.2 barg versus 11 barg design with flow unmeasured; firewater delivery is suspect, and partner readiness is unverified after its earlier first-attempt start failure.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect pump and test-line valves; engineering to disposition, rectify findings, then verify pressure and flow against acceptance criteria. Check impairment deviation record. Test pressure and flow to criteria. Verify partner pump readiness.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Below-design running pressure is meaningful degradation, but unknown acceptance criteria and unmeasured flow do not confirm loss of required delivery.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of firewater delivery would degrade a safety-critical fire-protection layer. The N+1 partner cannot be credited as currently capable because its earlier test had a failed first start despite later achieving rated pressure.

tickets.summary: Loose, wind-flapping cladding on the second-stage discharge has no reported process concern but may detach as a dropped object; personnel exposure below is unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Establish a drop zone; inspect attachment extent, secure or replace loose cladding, and verify retention. Check drop zone and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Active wind-driven movement and the explicit expectation that the cladding will become a dropped object support strong near-term progression, without confirming detachment has occurred.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Detachment creates a credible dropped-object injury hazard. Consequence cannot be bounded higher because cladding size, drop height and personnel exposure are not supplied; no process concern is reported.
